media_work.title: The Trials of Curtis Flowers (48 Hours)

media_item.item_title: The Trials of Curtis Flowers (48 Hours)
media_item.focus_or_theme: Multiple trials for the same crime, prosecutorial misconduct (racial bias in jury selection), impact of investigative journalism (podcast).
media_item.summary_notes: Curtis Flowers' case is exceptionally well-known due to the six trials, the Supreme Court ruling on racial bias in jury selection (*Flowers v. Mississippi*), and the critical role of the "In the Dark" podcast in exposing flaws. It is highly likely 48 Hours covered this case, focusing on the repeated trials and eventual release.

featured_individuals.time_served: Nearly 23 years (incarcerated from 1997-2020, mostly on death row)
featured_individuals.sentence: Death Penalty (in trials resulting in conviction)
featured_individuals.crime_convicted_of_raw: Capital Murder (quadruple homicide at Tardy Furniture store in 1996)
featured_individuals.narrative_summary: Curtis Flowers was tried six times for capital murder between 1997 and 2010, with multiple convictions overturned. He was exonerated in 2020 after serving nearly 23 years. His case was marked by persistent prosecutorial misconduct and was investigated by the "In the Dark" podcast.
contributing_factors_raw: Persistent prosecutorial misconduct (esp. racially biased jury selection documented by SCOTUS)
Focus of "In the Dark" podcast investigation highlighting flaws
